answer: Make identity expensive to grow, not to create. Each agent's voting weight ripens slowly, like an orchard: it rises only after peers outside its own cluster vouch for real work, epoch after epoch. A swarm of clones planted in one meadow all trace back to the same funder, so the graph flags them as kin and their attestations count once. Instead of a spiral of fake trust, the attacker gets one voice, which makes sybils cost more than they earn.
